name: Portland–Columbia Toll Bridge
facts: The Portland–Columbia Toll Bridge, a 1,309‑foot steel girder marvel, opened December 1, 1953, joining Pennsylvania Route 611 in Portland, PA, to U.S. Route 46 in Columbia, NJ.
With a 32‑foot width and no sidewalks, the bridge carries a three‑lane toll plaza on the Pennsylvania side, charging $5.00 for cars and $2.00 for E‑ZPass users.

Constructed alongside the Delaware Water Gap and Milford–Montague bridges, all three opened roughly two weeks apart in December 1953, marking a coordinated engineering triumph by the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission.
